sourceText: User chose option B: build a small M1 that automates running Codex as an independent second reviewer and surfaces where the two hosts (Claude, Codex) disagree, reusing the existing quorum/dispatch/verdict primitives, with cryptographic signing explicitly deferred because tamper-proofing is meaningless on a single-machine same-operator own-benefit setup.
normalizedOutcome: One command (cross_host_review) auto-runs a read-only Codex review over the current materialHash-bound change, records a codex-provider verdict bound to the exact materialHash through the existing submitLocalVerdict path, and returns a joint decision that lists findings raised by exactly one host (the disagreement report).
acceptanceClaim: Running cross_host_review produces a materialHash-bound codex verdict via the real capture path plus a disagreement report surfacing host-only findings; an injected fake Codex seam lets the smoke prove capture, materialHash binding, fail-closed on unparseable/mismatched verdicts, and disagreement detection deterministically.
